children: British asset manager Jupiter Fund Management
reported higher third-quarter net inflows on Thursday, helped by improving client demand and stronger flows across its investment strategies.
Net inflows totalled £700 million ($926.31 million) in the third quarter, compared with £300 million a year earlier, reversing second-quarter outflows of £800 million
Improving investor sentiment and demand for greater geographic diversification supported flows during the quarter, helping offset market volatility linked to renewed tensions in the Middle East
The update extends a recovery in client demand after Jupiter recorded its first year of positive net inflows since 2017 in 2025
Assets under management rose 51% to a record £75.9 billion at September 30, compared with £50.4 billion a year earlier
Retail, wholesale and investment trust net inflows reached £1.0 billion, marking a fifth consecutive quarter of positive flows
